AddCmd_HelpText:
How to create a voice command:

1) Command phrase — the exact word or phrase you say to run the command. Example: comma, new line, undo.

2) Action type — what happens when you say the phrase:
• Type text — types whatever you put in “Action value” (letters, punctuation, symbols).
• Send key — presses a key or shortcut on the keyboard.
• Switch to Persian / Switch to English — changes the keyboard layout.

3) Action value:
• Type text: the exact text to type. Examples:  ,  .  ?  or  Best regards
• Send key: press “Press a key…” and then press the key or combination itself — Enter, Tab, F5, Ctrl+C, Alt+F4. There is no code to write.

Tip: keep each phrase short and distinct so it is recognized reliably, and avoid a phrase that is a common word in ordinary dictation.
AddCmd_KeyHint: Click “Press a key…”, then press the key you want. Hold Ctrl, Alt or Shift at the same time for a combination.
AddCmd_KeyNotRecognized: Cloudict cannot send that key. Try a letter, a digit, a function key, or one of Enter, Tab, Space, Backspace, Delete, Escape, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down and the arrows.
AddCmd_PhraseTooltip: The word or phrase that triggers the command when spoken

Settings_SelectorsHelp: Cloudict recognizes speech by driving the Google Translate web page, so these selectors tell it where the microphone button and the source-text box are. You normally don't need to change them. If recognition or the automatic microphone-reset stops working — e.g. after Google changes the page, or when you switch the typing language — open Google Translate in Chrome, press F12, right-click the microphone (or text) element, choose "Inspect", and copy its identifier (jsname / class / aria-label) into the matching field below.
Settings_SelectorsHint: These values identify the microphone button and text box on the Google Translate page. If Google changes its design, just update these values.
Settings_ShortcutsFooter: Shortcuts work in every Windows app. By default Ctrl+Alt+A toggles the microphone and Ctrl+Alt+S stops it.
Settings_ShowIndicator: Show the microphone badge in the corner of the screen
Settings_StartDelayHint: Wait after the first words before auto-typing begins. Suggested 1500–3000 ms — higher on slow internet.
Settings_StartDelay_Tip: Why this exists: after you start speaking, Cloudict waits this long before it begins typing into your target app, giving Google Translate time to settle the first few words (which it revises the most) so they transfer correctly and properly spaced. On slow internet, give it more time. Too short means the first words may be wrong or run together; too long means typing starts late. Suggested 1500–3000 ms.
Settings_Subheading: Configure behavior, shortcuts and voice commands
Settings_TestSelectorsHint: After changing selectors, be sure to verify them with the “Test selectors” button.
Settings_TimingFooter: These delays are tuned to work correctly with Google Translate. If text is typed late or incompletely, increase the word-by-word delay first.
Settings_TimingHint: These delays keep Cloudict in sync with Google Translate. Hover over each field to see exactly what it does and why it matters. Keep values roughly between 50 and 5000 milliseconds.
Settings_TypingLanguageHint: The language you will speak; it configures the engine (e.g. the Google Translate page).
Settings_UnsavedConfirm: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to exit?
Settings_VoiceCommandsFooter: Voice command behavior depends on Google Translate being active and on speech recognition accuracy.
Settings_VoiceCommandsHint: Voice commands let you insert punctuation or trigger special keys by speaking keywords.
Settings_VoiceResetDone: Voice commands have been reset to defaults successfully.
Settings_WarningText: Voice commands work best with at most two words; pause briefly after announcing each command.
Settings_WordDelayHint: Wait before typing each word so Google can finalize it. Suggested 500–1000 ms — increase on slow/weak internet so words aren't typed before Google corrects them.
Settings_WordDelay_Tip: Why this exists: while you keep speaking, Google Translate often REVISES a word it just showed once it hears the next one (it corrects its first guess). So Cloudict waits this long before typing each word, to type the corrected/final word instead of the wrong first guess. On slow or weak internet Google needs more time, so increase this. Too short means wrong or partial words; too long means typing lags behind. Suggested 500–1000 ms.

SystemAudio_HelperSteps:
1) Open the download page below and download {0}.
2) Unzip it, right-click the setup for your Windows (x64) and choose "Run as administrator".
3) Press Install Driver, then restart the machine when asked.
4) Come back here and press "I have installed it".

Nothing else needs configuring — Cloudict switches the recording device over while the mode is on and puts it back afterwards.
